bullets.title: INTC: Multiple Downgrades, PT Cuts on PC Collapse + Fab Issues; Q4 Guide Misses Big
bullets.body: Intel's Q4 guide of $15-16B and $0.25 EPS missed consensus of $17.0B/$0.45 badly. PC unit volumes tracked -25% y/y in 2H26 with 2027 PC TAM expected down another -10%; a Fab 28 Israel explosion adds ~$300M revenue impact in Q4/Q1. DCAI grew +78% y/y but is supply-constrained. BofA and Roth cut to Neutral (PTs $100 and $70 respectively); Seaport and multiple others followed. INTC was down ~25% on Oct 30 open.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS Guides 40%+ in '27-'28 but 3Q Miss on AWS, Retail Drives -7% Premarket
bullets.body: Amazon's Q3 AWS grew 39.3% to $45.98B—below buyside bogey of 42-43%—but management guided 40%+ AWS growth in both 2027 and 2028, the first time Amazon issued specific future-year guidance. AWS backlog grew $82B q/q to $578B. Q3 capex of $77.3B was 31.7% above consensus. Q4 operating income guide ($28.5-33.5B midpoint) was ~$1.5B below consensus. Hedgeye is a strong buy with $342B 2028 AWS target; Goldman cut PT to $370.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Search Misses (-12% vs -14% expected); AI Mode Monetization Headwind; Stock -12% on Week
bullets.body: Alphabet's Q3 Search grew only 12% vs expectations of 14-15%, with AI Mode queries driving lower monetization per search. Google Cloud grew 103% y/y and YouTube Music/Premium reached 150M subs, but advertising shortfall drove a large EPS miss. Citi cut PT to $375 from $447 (Buy maintained); JPM and MS also trimmed targets. Stock fell ~12.6% on the week, the largest T+1 earnings day decline on record for Alphabet.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure +48% Beats Consensus; Guides +49-50% Next Q; $25B Bond Issuance
bullets.body: Microsoft's F1Q27 Azure grew 48% cc, beating the ~44% consensus and guiding F2Q to 49-50%. Commercial RPO reached $677B. Copilot daily users rose ~50% q/q. Operating margins came in near 50%. Separately, MSFT issued $25B in bonds—its first IG deal since 2017—and offered voluntary buyouts to ~60,000 employees. Goldman raised MSFT PT; stock held well relative to peers.

bullets.title: RDDT: Google AI Mode Drives ~1M/Week Search Referral Loss; DAU Risk LDD% in Q4
bullets.body: Reddit Q3 revenue beat by 8% with ad growth +54% y/y, but Google AI Mode disruption is cutting ~1M users/week in search referrals, risking low-double-digit sequential DAU decline in Q4. Reddit is pivoting to a logged-in-only platform (>80% of monetization from logged-in users). Citi cut PT to $186 from $245 (Buy maintained); Raymond James cut to $150 (Strong Buy). Opco downgraded to Perform.

bullets.title: SNDK: Beat-and-Raise; 50% of FY27 Bits Under Contract; 8-for-1 Split Nov 20
bullets.body: SanDisk September quarter revenue of $11.03B beat guidance ($10.3-10.8B) by ~7%; EPS $49.51 beat $46.67 consensus. Data Center now ~45% of revenue. Gross margins hit 85.1%. F2Q27 guide of $12.2-12.6B sales was well above consensus. NBM pipeline exceeds available supply through end of decade, with ~50% of FY27 bits and 67% of FY28 bits under long-term agreements. Company announced 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov 19/20. Citi maintains Buy, $2,100 PT.

bullets.title: RBLX: 3Q Bookings Beat but 4Q Guide -10 to -15% YoY; GTA VI Risk + AI Costs
bullets.body: Roblox Q3 bookings beat consensus by 4%; 4Q bookings guided $1.89-2.0B (below Street $2.0B high end) and 4Q covenant EBITDA $320-380M was 12% below consensus mid-point. GTA VI launching mid-4Q is a cited risk. Citi cut PT to $55 from $60 (Buy maintained) valued at 28x 2028 FCF.

bullets.title: DASH: Acquires CART for ~$17B; Strong 3Q Core Orders +17%; Citi $255 PT
bullets.body: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart for ~$17B (~$65/share, 75% cash/25% stock), adding 2,220+ retail partners and 26M annual orderers to accelerate its GnR business. Q3 core orders grew 17% y/y; U.S. restaurant GOV hit its fastest growth in five years. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 10bps to 3.12% of GOV. Deal expected to close 2H27/1H28; potential $500M+ annual synergies. JPM suspended ratings as financial advisor; Citi reiterates Buy $255 PT.

bullets.title: META: $95B+ Equity Raise Clears Capex Overhang; 3Q Beat; Stock -15% on Month
bullets.body: Meta priced a $35B common share offering plus up to $60B ATM starting Q1 2027, with NVDA, AMD, and AVGO each subscribing ~$5B. Q3 revenue grew 26.1% y/y, beating consensus by ~$1.3B. FY26 capex was narrowed to $135-145B. Meta is targeting $211B in CY27 capex for Muse AI and international capacity. Despite the strong quarter, META fell ~15.2% in October on AI financing concerns. Hedgeye and Citi remain constructive; Hedgeye keeps it a Top Long.

bullets.title: NOW: 3Q Slight Miss on cRPO; 4Q Guide Deceleration to 18.5% Drives -17% to -20% Drop
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 revenues were $4.11B (+0.5% beat) but cRPO grew only 20.3% vs buyside expecting 22%. Q4 cRPO guided at 18.5% cc—the sharpest step-down in the disclosed series. AI ACV target raised to $1.7B (+70% YTD) but organic subscription growth ex-Armis tracked to ~18-19%, flat with FY25. Non-GAAP subscription gross margin fell 300bps to 80.2%. Goldman maintains Buy; multiple analysts cut PTs. Hedgeye kept NOW on Long Bench.

bullets.title: ORCL: Investor Day Clears AI Funding Fear; FCF Positive 2H28; $30B+ FY29 FCF Target
bullets.body: Oracle's Investor Day revealed it will raise only ~$20B additional capital through FY30 (vs prior ~$60B fear), with FCF turning positive 2H FY28 and targeting >$30B in FY29. FY30 revenue target is $225B+ at 40%+ operating margins. Peak capex in FY27/28 then steps down. RPO stands at $664B with >90% tied to infrastructure. Stock rallied ~11% on the week. Citi raised PT to ORCL Buy; GS also constructive.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: Marvell in Advanced Talks to Acquire Lumentum; All-Stock at Modest Premium
bullets.body: Marvell is reportedly in advanced discussions to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal at a 'not all that large a premium,' with an announcement possible as soon as the week of Nov 3. LITE is sold out through 2029 and growing 40-60% annually. Wolfe sees strategic rationale but questions deal timing at peak valuations (LITE at 30x LTM rev). Morgan Stanley rates MRVL Equal-weight, citing integration risk. MRVL fell ~11%, LITE rose ~7-9% on the news.

bullets.title: AVGO: Upgrades, $63B Anthropic Financing Deal Backstopped; AI Capex Cycle Re-Affirmed
bullets.body: Broadcom arranged a $63B debt financing package for Anthropic's TPU chip procurement over five years—the largest AI infrastructure debt deal ever. AVGO provides residual value guarantees on $45B of the facility. DA Davidson upgraded AVGO to Buy ($400 PT). The deal, alongside Meta's equity raise and SpaceX's $40B GPU deal, drove the AI trade to bounce ~6.5% on semis/memory in the week of Oct 27. Wolfe views this as strong evidence that CY27-28 AI compute spending is likely to proceed.

bullets.title: CLS (Celestica): +17% on Massive 2027 Revenue Guide of $40B (+90% YoY); Top AI Server Play
bullets.body: Celestica posted Q3 EPS of $3.30 vs $2.96 consensus on $5.83B revenue. More importantly, it guided FY27 revenue to $40B (Street was $35.9B)—a 90% YoY increase—with 9% operating margins and EPS $21.50 (vs $20.83 consensus). Top customers are GOOGL (~35%), META (~17%), and AWS (~14%). 2028 revenues guided 'meaningfully above' 2027. FCF is expected positive in 2028. Citi raised PT to $436 (Buy).

bullets.title: EQIX: Record $533M Quarterly Bookings; MS Names Top Pick on 49GW Power Shortfall
bullets.body: Equinix reported record gross bookings of $533M in Q3 (+35% y/y) with new-deal pricing gains of +12%. Morgan Stanley named EQIX its Top Pick among data center REITs with a $1,250 PT (OW), citing a projected 49GW US power shortfall by 2028. DLR also reported record $627M bookings and raised FY guidance to ~13% core FFO/share growth; MS raised DLR PT to $215 but prefers EQIX.

bullets.title: GEV: Strong Beat/Raise; +96% Organic Orders; $9B Trench Acquisition; $20B Buyback
bullets.body: GE Vernova Q3 EPS beat FactSet consensus; orders grew +96% organically with power EBITDA margin at 21.4%. GEV raised FY26 guidance with adj EBITDA margin guide 13.5-14.5%, FCF $16-17B, and revenue $46.5-47.5B. GEV agreed to acquire Trench Group for $9B (13x '28 adj EBITDA). The company increased its buyback authorization from $10B to $20B. Roth and VRT both rallied in sympathy.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY GGR +67% YoY on Hold Expansion; October MTD GGR +36%; UBS Buy $48 PT
bullets.body: DraftKings NY handle fell -7% YoY in the week ending Oct 25 but GGR surged +67% YoY as hold rate expanded +510bps to 11.6%. October MTD GGR is tracking +36% YoY. DraftKings' NY market share stands at 32.4-32.5%. FanDuel and Caesars also saw strong GGR due to hold expansion. UBS maintains Buy with $48 PT based on 17x 2028E EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: FSLR: Q3 EPS Beat but Cuts '26 Guidance; Section 232 Delays Pricing Inflection
bullets.body: First Solar Q3 EPS of $5.30 beat FactSet $4.67 but cut 2026 revenue, EBITDA, volume, and capex guidance. US ASPs at 36c/W missed expectations; booking inflection pushed out to mid-2027 as developers face tariff, permitting, and interconnection issues. Board authorized $500M buyback. GLJ Research downgraded to Hold ($161 PT); MS cut PT to $307 (Overweight maintained); Roth kept Buy at $300.

bullets.title: ENPH: Q4 Guide -20% vs Consensus; Downgraded Multiple Times; US Solar Demand Weak
bullets.body: Enphase Q3 EPS of $0.41 missed FactSet $0.51; Q4 revenue guided $225-255M vs consensus $297.6M with gross margin 40-43%. Management cited weak US residential solar demand, Europe softness (France -12% sell-through), and battery storage margin pressure from price cuts. Roth and Oppenheimer downgraded to Neutral/Perform. SEDG fell 9% in sympathy.

bullets.title: FOXA: Added to BofA US 1 List; Strong Setup into Q1 Earnings Nov 2
bullets.body: BofA added Fox Corp to its US 1 List ahead of Q1 earnings on Nov 2. Consensus expects $4.32B revenue and $2.08 EPS, with the stock up 8.3% since August and beating revenue consensus 17 of the last 20 quarters. Citi also ranks Fox as its #1-rated media stock, noting the planned Roku acquisition closing Q1 2027 should be accretive to FCF per share in year 1. Options imply ~8.3% move.
